verdicts.argument: At 43 this is the largest class and it is large because it is glue, not mechanism. Three unrelated defenses are stapled together — the gate_idea itself lists three: an enum cartesian-product harness, a URL-reachability probe, and an imperative-copy-to-control lint. Those land on different people, in different files, at different phases. Worse, the backend half ('an outcome enum is persisted but no executor stamps executedAt') is not distinguishable in review from class 3's 'a new status is written while sibling consumers keep the old set' — same enum, same file, same fix (exhaustiveness over the enum). And the nutribuddy#113 exemplar (a state table in a TEST that omits creating-recipe/recipe-error) is not this class at all; it is verification-bound-to-a-proxy — a contract test that cannot go red for a missing state. Exemplar leakage of that size means the boundary is not operative.
verdicts.replacement: Split into (1a) 'variant admitted by a writer with no terminal path' — every value a writer can persist must have an executor/consumer that reaches a terminal state, gate = enum cartesian product + committed UNSUPPORTED_VARIANTS file; and (1b) 'advertised affordance with nothing behind it' — copy, a link, an emitted URL, a fallback, or an error branch promises an action for which no control, route, or handler exists in any subtree, gate = imperative-string-to-handler lint + emitted-URL-resolves-to-registered-route probe. Then merge (1a) with class 3's first half into one exhaustiveness class; reassign nutribuddy#113 to verification-bound-to-a-proxy.

verdicts.argument: The mechanism is genuinely sharp — 'the two sides resolve the name through different machinery' is the distinguishing clause and it does transfer. But every word of the class as written is Docker/Compose/Vercel/GitHub-Actions vocabulary, and the gate is five stack-specific shell commands (`docker compose -f A config`, `vercel env ls`, `apps/api/src`). Nothing in it transfers to a repo on a different platform, so a reader on another stack will conclude the class does not apply to them. Second defect: the boundary against class 10 is undefined. Both are 'two sides encode independently'; the operative difference (identifier resolution vs. duplicated semantic rule) is stated nowhere a triaging reviewer will find it, so findings will land in whichever class is read first.
verdicts.replacement: Restate at the general altitude: 'an identifier is produced by one artifact and consumed by another, and the two resolve it through different mechanisms (build-time substitution vs. runtime lookup vs. literal vs. platform interpolation vs. dashboard registration), so a human diff reads identical and the runtime objects differ.' Gate stated generically as: enumerate every identifier crossing an artifact boundary; for each, assert a reader exists, assert a writer exists, and assert the two resolution mechanisms are the same — with the compose/vercel/Actions commands demoted to a stack-specific appendix. Add an explicit disambiguation line: this class is identifiers; class 10 is shapes and predicates.

verdicts.argument: The class claims one gate closes both directions and that claim is false on its own text. Direction (a), 'a new enum value is not propagated to sibling readers', is closed by exhaustiveness (Record<Enum,T> / never-default) — a type-system fix. Direction (b), 'a new operator or bulk endpoint performs the transition with its own inline update and skips the canonical method's side effects', is closed by a single-writer-per-transition AST assertion plus a post-condition equivalence suite — a call-graph fix. Those are independent defenses; a repo can pass one and fail the other completely. They also have different root causes: (a) is a missing type, (b) is a missing owner for a transition. Folding coachflow-1 `control-registered-but-not-in-execution-path` in here too (per the dropped notes) is a third thing again (a declared guard absent from the DI graph).
verdicts.replacement: Split into (3a) 'the value set is enumerated at each call site instead of carried by an exhaustive type' — merge this with class 1a into one exhaustiveness class; and (3b) 'a state transition has more than one writer, so the non-canonical writer omits its side effects' — gate = one whitelisted transition function per status, asserted by AST, plus a suite driving every route that reaches the status and asserting identical post-conditions. Move the guard-not-in-providers case to (3b) as 'declared control absent from the execution graph' or split it out at recurrence 3.

verdicts.argument: The title names one mechanism (misclassified error → wrong durability decision) but the exemplars carry at least two more. The orphaned object-storage upload, `emitAsync` inside a serializable transaction, and abandonUpload deleting bytes while the metadata row stays active have nothing to do with classifying an error — they fail even when the error is perfectly classified, because there is no unit of commit across two stores and no compensating action. Conversely the timeout-recorded-as-rejection case fails even with a perfect saga. The gates confirm the split: fault injection with {terminal, timeout-after-success, timeout-before-send} tests classification; a compensating-action inventory and a ban on non-tx clients inside a transaction callback tests atomicity. Also, `set -e` skipping a rollback is a third medium (shell control flow) that neither lint reaches.
verdicts.replacement: Split into (4a) 'an ambiguous failure is recorded as a definite outcome' — timeouts, partial provider responses, and catch-all filters collapsing a failure space onto one meaning before a durability/ack decision; gate = fault injection asserting external-effect count === 1 and a lint requiring every catch in a payment/webhook path to rethrow, persist a retry source, or carry an AMBIGUOUS-SAFE annotation. And (4b) 'a multi-store mutation has no unit of commit and no compensating action' — including the shell/process-exit variant where the control-flow construct skips the compensation; gate = compensating-action inventory per external mutation, ban on non-transactional clients inside transaction callbacks, and a chaos job for the deploy path.

verdicts.argument: The best-formed class here. It is unambiguously a mechanism, not a topic; the asymmetry framing ('these checks can never go red, so nobody notices they are decorative') is the property that makes it detectable; and it transfers to any stack because the medium (deploy gate, unit test, contract probe, workflow filter) is explicitly declared irrelevant. The negative-fixture-matrix gate is the single strongest gate in the taxonomy and generalizes without modification. One correction: the luxebook#67 paths-filter exemplar is double-filed — class 14 claims the same defect with the same defense (compute the transitive import graph, compare to the declared paths). Assign it to 14 and keep this class to assertions that inspect the wrong subject. Also note the taxonomy's own merge rationale here ('deploy gates, unit tests and path filters differ only in medium') is inconsistent with keeping class 16 separate; the defensible reason 16 stays separate is its propagation behavior, not its medium — say so explicitly in both classes.

The core (a condition established by a prior read is absent from the write predicate, so any interleaving or elapsed time is undetectable) is excellent and the SSI one-way-rw-dependency detail is the kind of thing that earns a class its existence. But the merge that absorbed `tenant-scope-omitted-on-write-or-contract` is wrong for a large subset of the corpus. 'Write profile updates to authenticated owner', 'Use the body guestId when no guest cookie exists', 'Avoid creating guest sessions from unrelated cookies', 'Route guest setup work to the landing owner' are not races: they fail on the FIRST request with no concurrency at all, because the subject of the write was supplied by the caller rather than derived from the authenticated principal. Calling that a stale-precondition problem tells the implementer to add a CAS predicate, when the actual fix is never to accept the subject from the request. Different failure model, different gate, different threat.
verdicts.replacement: Keep the TOCTOU core as-is (including the tenant-compound-key case, where a tenant-scoped read is genuinely followed by an id-only write). Split off 'authorization subject supplied by the caller rather than derived from the authenticated principal' — the write names an owner/guest/tenant/actor id that arrived in the body, query, or an unrelated cookie and was never checked against the session; gate = lint banning any owner/actor/tenant identifier in a write's where/data whose provenance is the request payload rather than the resolved principal, plus a cross-actor E2E asserting A's identifier in B's request is rejected, not honored.

verdicts.argument: The mechanism is real and well-observed but the title and framing pin it to browser sessions, which is a topic. The general shape — replicated state with several independent writers, no designated authority, and no writer asserting the SUBJECT of what it persists — is exactly what class 17's PostHog exemplars are (identity in SDK state + auth provider + tenant tag, cleared on only one path), what the cached-role entitlement finding is, and what any multi-copy state does. Stated at session altitude, this class will not fire on the next instance that isn't a session, and its exemplars are already leaking into 17. Second problem: 'a lifecycle leg is missing per carrier' (clearCookie omitting set-time attributes, failed verify rewriting a fresh TTL) is a checklist item, not the same mechanism as 'no authority' — it belongs as a sub-shape with its own attribute-parity assertion.
verdicts.replacement: Restate as 'replicated state with multiple independent writers and no designated authority' — for each copy: who may write it, what generation/subject token accompanies the write, which copy wins on disagreement, and what clears it. Sessions become the dominant instance; telemetry identity, cached role/entitlement, and cross-tab copies stop needing a separate home. Keep the multi-context interleaving suite as the gate and add the general assertion 'after every interleaving, all carriers agree on the subject'. Pull the per-carrier lifecycle legs (set/clear attribute parity, expiry, subject binding) out as a named sub-checklist with its own mechanical assertion.

verdicts.argument: Distinct, correctly separated from the precondition class, and the separation argument given ('the condition is missing from the write predicate' vs 'there is no unique claim for the effect' need different storage primitives) is right. The identity dimension — too fine (per-attempt random key) vs too coarse (key that does not change per logical event) — is a genuine second failure direction that shares the single defense 'name the storage operation that makes one caller the winner, and persist the key before the effect', so it is not a split. Transfers to any stack: unique index, conditional update, SET NX with owner token, GETDEL are primitives, not framework features. Only nit: the two-writers-computing-different-lock-keys case is arguably class 2 (a name resolved by two different builders); leave it here since the consequence is a missing claim, but cross-reference it.

Two directions are declared in the mechanism text and they share nothing but the word 'generation'. Direction (a), 'the old artifact survives and WINS', is a provisioning/precedence problem: a surviving drop-in, a host-only cookie ordered first, a webhook endpoint still registered in a vendor dashboard. Its gate is idempotent-rerun testing and a repo-plus-external-registry grep for the old value. Direction (b), 'existing rows cannot satisfy the new constraint', is a data-migration problem: a column added without a backfill, a validator tightened against a population never enumerated. Its gate is a legacy fixture dataset and a migration lint. Different artifacts, different phases, different owners, zero shared assertion. The one thing they share — 'the predecessor inventory was drawn from memory' — is the taxonomy's most-repeated meta-observation (it is also classes 1, 13 and 14's root) and is too thin to be a class boundary on its own.
verdicts.replacement: Split into (9a) 'the predecessor artifact survives and takes precedence' — surviving units/drop-ins, unexpired cookies, live hostnames, third-party registrations held outside the repo; gate = run provisioning twice with a rotated value and assert no artifact contains the first value, plus a cutover preflight that generates the checklist from a grep over repo AND external registries rather than by hand. And (9b) 'a constraint lands before the population or the write path that can satisfy it' — backfill-less migrations, tightened validators, gates enforced before any actor can comply; gate = migrations adding a canonicalized/NOT NULL column must contain a backfill or a pre-migration-shaped fixture test, plus a permanently checked-in legacy dataset in E2E.

verdicts.argument: Three mechanisms wearing one title. (i) A business rule is hand-copied on both sides of a wire (client eligibility predicate vs server guard) — fix: one exported predicate. (ii) A validator's admitted set differs from the sink's accepted set (@IsOptional skipping null while the service branches on undefined, `new Date(null)` writing 1970) — this is not two sides re-encoding a rule at all; it is a library whose documented semantics were assumed, i.e. class 12. (iii) A response is cast rather than parsed (`await res.json() as T`, DTO fields the server never sends, wrong HTTP verb) — no second encoding exists here either; nothing verifies the wire at all. Three gates are already listed for the three: shared predicate module, decorator lint, schema parse. Also, like class 2, the whole class is written in NestJS/class-validator/Prisma vocabulary and needs generalizing.
verdicts.replacement: Split into (10a) 'a rule is enforced independently on both sides of a boundary and the client's copy is always the simpler one' — buttons that always 4xx, limits that pass locally and fail at the sink, orderings that disagree; gate = one exported predicate consumed by both, plus a Playwright matrix asserting 'enabled control implies 2xx'. And (10b) 'a value crossing a boundary is asserted rather than validated' — casts without a parse, declared fields the producer never sends, verbs and shapes taken from memory instead of from the producer's own types; gate = ban unchecked casts on parsed wire data, generate client types from the producer's schema, contract fuzz asserting 400-not-500 and never 2xx-with-mutation. Move the @IsOptional/null-semantics case to class 12 (library semantics assumed), where its gate already lives.

verdicts.argument: The strongest genuinely-new class in the set — existing_rule is honestly reported as 'none' and the mechanism (capture the subject at intent time vs. re-derive it at execution time from a mutable parent) is a real distinction no other class states. It transfers unmodified to any deferred-execution system: job queues, outbox rows, webhooks, sweeps, scheduled mail. The sub-shapes hold together under the same question: recycled row across lifecycles, live-read seller config, current connected-account id, and composite identity compared on one component are all 'the subject or the terms were re-derived later'. The 'single-generation happy paths always resolve to the only row, so tests never see it' observation is exactly the kind of thing that tells an implementer why their test suite is silent. Only refinement: state the anchoring rule as a positive invariant ('every deferred row stores the id of the external object, the account that created it, and the generation boundary') so it is checkable at write time rather than only at execution time.

'Third-party and framework' is a SOURCE, not a mechanism, and 'assumed rather than probed' is an epistemic stance that could be prefixed to any class in this document. What is inside is at least three distinct mechanisms: (i) a value the producer emits for several causes is mapped onto one internal meaning (window.open returning null on success, Charge.refunds absent unless expanded, a $0 trial invoice.paid) — genuine, sharp, and general beyond vendors; (ii) delivery guarantees assumed (at-least-once, unordered) — the defect and the fix are identical to classes 8 and 4a (idempotent apply, monotonic writes), so this belongs there, not here; (iii) framework composition order (basePath prepended twice, rewrites vs middleware ordering, @OnEvent not awaiting, render-body access to localStorage/clock) — that is a composition/topology problem adjacent to class 2, not a semantics problem. Additionally the proposed gate ('a recorded probe artifact that demonstrates the assumed behavior') is the same gate as class 5's negative fixture, which is a sign the class is being held together by its remedy rather than its mechanism.
verdicts.replacement: Split into (12a) 'an external value is many-to-one and is read as one-to-one' — the code branches on a value the producer emits for several causes, or on a projection the producer truncates/omits by default; gate = for every external value branched on, a recorded quote from the producer's types or docs plus the enumerated other causes, and vendor-fixture replay for absent/truncated/duplicate/reordered cases. And (12b) 'two layers each apply the same transformation, or the composition order is assumed' — double-prefixed paths, rewrites vs middleware, hooks that do not await, render-time access to environment-specific globals; gate = route-topology test against the BUILT app asserting each declared client target resolves to the intended handler. Reassign the delivery-guarantee exemplars to classes 8 and 4a.

verdicts.argument: Survives on the strength of its gate. The mechanism sentence — the control's domain is hand-enumerated while the surface is defined by the vendor's transport list, payload schema, or the browser's degraded behavior — is a mechanism, and the recurrence tell ('each round names one more carrier the list forgot, and the fix adds exactly that one name') is what makes it non-closable by patching instances. The canary-at-every-leaf property test plus the outbound-body integration probe is a genuinely inverting gate: it drives the control from the schema instead of from memory, and new schema fields fail by default. Caveat to record in the class: this is the third appearance of one meta-mechanism (a hand-maintained set whose real membership is defined elsewhere) alongside classes 9 and 14, and the only thing keeping the three apart is that their gates are genuinely different. If any two of them ever converge on the same gate, they must merge. Also: the no-JS native GET exemplar is arguably a separate 'the transport chosen is not the transport the platform will actually use' shape; keep it here only because the same canary probe catches it.

The causality half and the credential half are unrelated. 'The declared input set is narrower than the real one' (needs DAG, workflow_run ancestry, path filters, turbo env lists, Dockerfile COPY sets) is one mechanism with one gate: derive the declaration from the real graph. 'Untrusted input interpolated into a shell string' and 'a token echoed unmasked into a log' is injection and secret handling — the defect is concatenation into an interpreter and unbounded credential blast radius, and its fixes (quoted env indirection, pinned host fingerprints, scoped secrets, preflight before the first remote side effect) share no assertion with the DAG check. Bundling them means a repo with a perfect needs-DAG reads as compliant while shell-interpolating a dispatch input. Also reclaim luxebook#67 (paths filter omitting the file the guarded behavior depends on) from class 5 — the same transitive-import-graph gate lives here.
verdicts.replacement: Split into (14a) 'the pipeline's declared input and causality set is narrower than the build's real one' — workflow_run ancestry, needs edges, path filters, cache key/env lists, image COPY sets; gate = build the DAG and the transitive import graph in CI and fail on any asymmetry, plus 'deploy must be a causal descendant of the job that tested THIS head_sha'. And (14b) 'an untrusted or secret value crosses into an interpreter, a log, or a wider blast radius than it needs' — this is a general class that also covers the app-side corpus (dispatch inputs into `run:`, whole prod env files attached to a one-variable container, unmasked ExecStart read-backs, and on the app side free-form user text concatenated into request headers and double-decoded query values); gate = ban direct interpolation of event/input expressions into interpreters, require encoding at every interpreter boundary, require preflight validation of every reachable secret before the first side effect, require pinned host fingerprints, and grep run logs for credential prefixes post-job.

verdicts.argument: The title makes accessibility the subject, which is a topic; the two mechanisms underneath are both more general and more valuable stated generally. (i) 'State carried by DOM node identity is destroyed by a subtree swap' is not an a11y fact — focus is one instance, but scroll position, uncontrolled input value, in-flight animation, media playback state and live-region continuity are the same defect, and the fix is the same shared phase wrapper. The luxebook#109 detail that the identical defect reappeared in the SECOND component of the same PR is the proof the fix belongs to the transition, not to the component. (ii) 'An adapter forwards only the props it was authored for, dropping capability the wrapped thing owns' is the general facade-narrowing defect — field.disabled and field.ref today, a repository wrapper dropping a transaction option or an SDK wrapper dropping retry config tomorrow. Two mechanisms, two gates (a transition assertion helper; a conformance suite over every wrapper against the wrapped library's own contract).
verdicts.replacement: Split into (15a) 'state carried by node identity is destroyed by a remount or subtree swap, silently' — focus, live-region continuity, scroll, uncontrolled values; gate = one shared assertion helper required for every async state machine (activeElement is not body after the trigger unmounts; the status node exists BEFORE the transition and only its text changes; axe on every state; dialogs trap and inert). And (15b) 'a wrapper narrows the contract of the thing it wraps' — the adapter forwards a subset of what the underlying library exposes, and the ids it generates are not referenced by the element that needs them; gate = a conformance suite over every export of the wrapper package driven from the wrapped library's own contract (render under disabled:true and assert disabled AND absent from submitted values; assert setFocus works; assert every generated id appears in the control's describedby).

verdicts.argument: Distinct despite the obvious objection that a doc is just another medium of class 5. The property that earns it its own class is the propagation mechanism, not the medium: a false claim in a designated-authoritative doc is consumed by later audits, agents and implementers as evidence the work is done, which converts a live defect into an invisible one and makes editing prose the cheapest possible way to close a review finding. Class 5's negative-fixture gate cannot touch that; the anchor-every-claim-to-file:line@sha gate can, and it is executable. The recurrence tell ('the same document is re-flagged round after round because each fix edits wording rather than code') is a real, observable signature. Two corrections: state explicitly why this is not class 5 (propagation to future agents, not false PASS of a check), and reassign the 'one spec defines two route names for one operation' exemplar — that is class 2 (a name encoded twice), with the doc merely being one of the encodings.

Holds together: every sub-shape answers the same implementer question ('what re-runs this once the value settles, without discarding user edits'), and the mechanism — a value consumed at a lifecycle moment when it is not yet or no longer authoritative — transfers past React to any system with an initialization window or a cached authorization answer. The latched-init-effect-with-a-deliberately-narrowed-dependency-list observation is precise and the required test pattern (mount with isLoading, flush, assert seeded state equals the loaded-first case AND typed text survives) is a real gate. Two fixes needed: the PostHog identify/reset exemplars are the multi-carrier-no-authority mechanism (class 7) wearing a timing costume — the reset-only-on-full-logout bug is a missing clear path, not a settling problem — so move them once class 7 is restated generally; and the render-time `now` sub-shape deserves its own named assertion (a boundary that passes while the page is open) because its fix is an interval/refetch, not a settle callback.

This is the taxonomy's riskiest merge and the title makes it worse. Timezone and design tokens do share an abstract shape, but the title says 'host default', which describes only the timezone half — a raw hex literal is not a host default, it is a bypassed authority, and a reader scanning titles will never file a color literal here. The merge is also lopsided in consequence: one half books a customer at a different instant than displayed (P1 correctness), the other half fails to propagate a palette change (consistency), and they carry different gates (ban the ambient date API + run the suite under two TZs; ban raw literals + resolve against the design source). Kept as-is, the class dilutes its own P1 signal. But the abstraction is worth keeping, because the corpus contains more instances than the two named — currency symbols derived from a default rather than from billing data, locale, units — and a two-instance class will not catch the third.
verdicts.replacement: Restate as 'a value has a designated authority and the call site reaches for the ambient or raw equivalent instead' — authorities enumerated explicitly (tenant timezone, tenant currency and locale, design tokens, unit systems, feature-flag source, shared shells), with the invariant 'the authority must be passed explicitly at every call site; a later change to the authority must reach every surface'. Carry a per-authority gate table rather than one gate: for time, ban the ambient date APIs in scheduling/calendar code and run the suite under two timezones requiring byte-identical results; for presentation, ban raw color/radius/shadow/tracking literals and resolve composition-locked pairs against the design source; for money and locale, ban symbol/format literals outside a formatter that takes the record's own currency. Rename so the title covers 'host default OR raw literal'.

missing_classes: Collected constraint never threaded to the consumer that must honor it — the largest unnamed cluster in the corpus (~40 nutribuddy findings: 'Apply dietary restrictions when building the deck', 'Carry guest restrictions into recipe generation', 'Wire guest preferences into card selection', 'Carry stored preferences into follow-up prompts', 'Apply guest safety preferences before loading cards', 'Re-check card safety when recording right swipes'). A value is captured, validated and persisted at one stage, and each downstream decision (ranking, filtering, prompt construction, a second write path, a migration) independently decides whether to read it — so the constraint is simply absent from the computation. This is not class 3 (there the rule exists at every call site in a stale form) and not class 1 (nothing is unreachable). Defense is different too: a single typed decision-input object that every consumer must accept, plus a test asserting each consumer's OUTPUT varies when the constraint varies. Safety-critical here: the dropped value is an allergy.

Two distinct domains collapsed into one field or flag — 'Do not treat goals as safety restrictions', 'Do not let noRestrictions bypass allergies', 'Allow goals alongside no restrictions', 'Include no-restrictions in preference detection'. One field carries both a soft preference and a hard safety constraint, so a code path written for one semantics silently applies to the other and a UI affordance for one clears the other. Distinct from the class above (the value arrives, but typed as the wrong thing) and from class 3 (no enum extension involved). Defense: separate the types so a preference cannot be passed where a constraint is required, and assert the safety filter is unreachable-by-construction from the preference path.

A stub, fake-mode, or fallback implementation is reachable in production and its output is indistinguishable from the real one — ~15 findings ('Require a real AI provider in production', 'Disallow fake signup in production runtime', 'Route auth form to active provider instead of fake fallback', 'Replace placeholder D1 database IDs before deploy', 'Rank by preference semantics instead of seed salt', 'Detect fake fallback behavior semantically, not by phrase'). The mechanism is that the degraded path fabricates a plausible result rather than failing, so no probe, log line or user report distinguishes it from the real path — and mode selection is spread across client env, server env and per-route defaults with no single authority. Related to but not covered by the existing silent-no-op-integrations note. Defense: production builds must fail closed on any stub binding; every fallback must be observable in its output or its response metadata; mode is resolved once, server-side, and asserted at boot.

Cache or memo key narrower than the variance of the value it caches, with no invalidation edge from the writers — 'Keep availability cache keys in UTC date space', 'Skip ISR caching for tenant 404 responses', 'Do not key active card responses by request order', 'Invalidate all affected day caches after late-decision updates', 'Refresh cached cards when re-entering swipes'. The key omits a dimension the response actually varies on (tenant, timezone, auth state, request ordering), or a writer mutates the underlying data with no edge to the entries it invalidates, so one tenant's negative result is served to another. Currently smeared across classes 2 (key drift) and 17 (staleness); neither names it and neither gate catches it. Defense: derive the key mechanically from the full input tuple the handler reads, forbid caching of tenant- or auth-scoped negative responses, and require every writer to name the cache entries it invalidates.

Authorization subject taken from caller-supplied input rather than from the authenticated principal — 'Write profile updates to authenticated owner', 'Use the body guestId when no guest cookie exists', 'Avoid creating guest sessions from unrelated cookies', 'Keep right-swipe handoff from reusing guest-owned chat IDs', 'Route guest setup work to the landing owner'. Mis-merged into precondition-read-outside-the-write, which frames it as a stale read; these fail on the first request with zero concurrency, and the fix is provenance (derive the subject from the resolved principal), not a CAS predicate.

An untrusted or unbounded value crosses into an interpreter or a length-limited transport — '${{ inputs.* }}' interpolated into a `run:` body, 'Bound guest allergy text before sending it as a header', 'Encode preferences before using a request header', 'Avoid double-decoding guest preference queries', 'Cap preference arrays before provider calls'. Currently a footnote inside class 14's credential half, but it is one general mechanism spanning CI shell, HTTP headers, URLs and provider payloads: the value is concatenated or serialized into a channel with its own grammar and its own hard limits, and neither the encoding nor the bound is applied at the boundary. Defense: encode at every interpreter boundary (never interpolate), bound at the producer, and decode exactly once with an asserted arity.

A runtime capability is assumed present rather than feature-detected against the declared support matrix — 'Avoid unsupported AbortSignal.timeout in the resolver' (undefined on Safari <16.4, so the entire browser-side recovery path throws before fetch and every Retry repeats the failure), request-scoped DI used where no request context exists, render-body access to storage APIs. Class 12 covers the SEMANTICS of an API the runtime has; this is the API not existing in part of the runtime matrix the project actually declares support for. Defense: lint modern APIs against the project's own browserslist/engines declaration, and require a feature-detected fallback on any path that exists to recover from failure.

The implementation ships a lookalike of the mandated structure rather than the structure — 'Implement the desktop split surface instead of wrapping mobile UI', 'Use the three-column Saved layout at 1280px', 'Size the setup from its containing shell', 'Keep desktop setup out of the mobile bottom sheet', 'Add the mandated design artifact before shipping these states'. Class 18 covers drifted VALUES (tokens, tracking), class 16 covers docs asserting what code does not enforce; neither covers code that satisfies the spec's description while delivering a different composition, nor the process failure where the authoritative artifact the spec is supposed to be checked against was never produced. Defense: the spec's structural claims are expressed as executable layout/composition assertions at the declared breakpoints, and a PR introducing customer-visible states without the mandated source artifact fails.

verdicts.argument: Recurrence 43 is the tell: this is an attractor that absorbs anything describable as 'no path forward', and its gate splinters into four unrelated checks — which is the operational definition of a topic rather than a mechanism. Test each piece against its own exemplar. (a) The enum cartesian-product harness DOES fail on coachflow#1 (ACCOUNT_CREDIT with executedAt null after the sweep drains) — but only after a human hand-authors per-cell fixtures, which is precisely the enumeration labor the gate claims to remove; what is actually mechanical is the completeness half, not the driving half. (b) 'grep every URL template emitted by notification templates and assert each resolves to a registered route' — templates are interpolated (`${base}/b/${id}/manage`), so the grep recovers a prefix, not a route, and passes on any interpolated segment; it also cannot fail on the cited coachflow#4 exemplar, where '/' IS a registered route and the defect is that the console layout bounces it. (c) 'lint pairing user-facing strings containing an imperative with a rendered control in the same subtree' is self-refuting twice over: detecting an imperative needs NLP, 'same subtree' needs a render graph across component boundaries, and the cited luxebook#1 exemplar is not a missing control at all — the credit-note control exists, it is just unreachable by that actor. No linter has that. Splitting also fixes the severity smear: the persisted-outcome half is where the ~9 P1s live, the UI half is P2 cosmetics-of-flow.
verdicts.replacement: Split into (1) `persisted-outcome-with-no-executor` — executable-strong, gated exactly like verify-mutation-claim-registry.mjs: reflect every persisted enum out of schema.prisma, require each member to appear in a committed `outcome-executors.json` as either {executor: 'symbolName'} or {unsupported: 'reason'}; fail when a member is unclassified, when a named executor symbol does not exist in the tree, or when an executor is named but never writes the terminal column. Nobody has to remember to ask, and the diff that adds PACKAGE_CREDIT breaks the build. (2) `reachable-ui-state-with-no-exit-affordance` — honest feasibility executable-partial. The only mechanical assertions are: every error/fallback branch component must be listed in a state-inventory fixture and rendered in a test that asserts at least one enabled interactive element or a link with an href resolving to a route in the generated route manifest; and every URL *prefix* literal handed to a client must resolve in that manifest. Drop the imperative-copy lint entirely — replace it with the implementer_question, which is a review prompt, not a gate.

verdicts.argument: The class is sound and the merge is right, but the gate bundle mixes the single best check in the whole taxonomy with a check that is exactly the failure mode the taxonomy condemns. Part (2), `docker compose -f A config` vs `-f B config` diffed on resolved volume names, is genuinely executable-strong: it uses Compose's own resolver rather than a grep, and it fails on coachflow#7 literally (coachflow_pgdata vs coachflow_coachflow_pg) and passes once the keys agree. Part (3) (bind sources vs git index) and part (4) (production-required env.schema keys must appear as `-e KEY=`) are likewise real; (4) fails on luxebook#85 provided the schema is a static literal — a computed/spread schema defeats the ts-morph read, so it needs a lint forbidding non-literal keys in env.schema. Part (1) is the problem: 'grep app source for readers — fail on any name with zero readers or any reader with zero writers'. Names are read dynamically (`process.env[k]`), inlined at build (NEXT_PUBLIC_*), or consumed by the platform and never by app source; this fires constantly on correct code, earns an allowlist within a week, and the allowlist then rots into the same hand-maintained inventory the class is about. It is a grep that matches the wrong thing in the false-positive direction. Also: the cookie-Domain / CORS-allowlist sub-shape (luxebook#88, coachflow#1) is not statically decidable at all — the deployed origin is not in the repo — so it cannot be part of a static gate.
verdicts.replacement: Keep parts (2)(3)(4)(5); drop part (1). Replace it with the tool-resolver pattern generalized: for every pair of artifacts claiming to describe the same environment, run each artifact's OWN resolver and diff the resolved output (compose config, `vercel env pull` vs env.schema keys, `docker buildx bake --print`), failing on any key resolving to different strings. Add one narrow mechanical rule for the tag case: if a workflow uses docker/metadata-action with `type=sha` and lacks `format=long`, no other workflow or run: body may reference `sha-${{ github.sha }}`. Move the cookie-Domain/CORS sub-shape out of the static gate and into a post-deploy runtime probe that asserts a Set-Cookie issued by the API is readable from the configured frontend origin — that assertion is bound to the behavior and can actually go red.

verdicts.argument: The headline gate cannot fail on the headline exemplar. `Record<BookingStatus, T>` plus a `never` default catches 'you forgot to MENTION the new member' — but luxebook#79 (startService writes IN_PROGRESS while completeBooking's guard admits only CONFIRMED/CHECKED_IN) is not a missing mention: IN_PROGRESS already existed in the enum, and `Record<BookingStatus, boolean>` with `IN_PROGRESS: false` compiles cleanly and is still exactly the shipped bug. Exhaustiveness is a gate against forgetting a key, never against a wrong value at a present key, and at least half these exemplars are the latter (the reporting.service filter, the confirmation-view badge map). Same for the 'ban inline status arrays, import from status-sets.ts' rule: it relocates the divergence into one file where a human can see it — valuable, but it makes nothing go red. What survives is the third piece, and it is genuinely strong and matches the proven registry pattern already on disk: an AST assertion that `prisma.*.update*` writing `status: <VALUE>` occurs only inside one whitelisted transition function per status. That fails on applyLateDecision writing status inline (luxebook#79) and on the generic 'new operator/bulk endpoint with its own update' direction, which is where the P1s are.
verdicts.replacement: Demote the exhaustive-Record/never claim from gate to refactor-precondition (it is what makes the real gate cheap to write, not itself a gate). Promote to executable-strong only: (i) single-writer-per-status AST registry — `status-writers.json` maps each status to exactly one transition function; any prisma write of that status outside it fails, and adding a status without an entry fails; (ii) a lint that status literals in a query `where` for models on a declared MONEY_OR_INVENTORY list must be identifiers imported from status-sets.ts (mechanical, failable, and it is what makes (i) auditable). Honest partial for the wrong-value-at-a-present-key direction: no static check reaches it — the only failable assertion is a post-condition suite that drives every route reaching each status and asserts identical post-conditions, and that suite must itself be under the mutation-testing regime from `verification-bound-to-a-proxy` or it becomes a decorative green.

verdicts.argument: Merged on mechanism, but the two halves need disjoint gates, and since the taxonomy exists to generate gates, gate-disjointness should govern the class boundary. Half one (partial multi-store write with no compensation) is statically gateable and the proposals work: 'forbid non-tx clients (this.prisma, storage, notificationService, emitAsync) inside a $transaction callback' is pure AST, fails on luxebook#94 exactly, and passes on the fix; the `set -e` shell rule, scoped to run: blocks in .github/workflows, fails on luxebook#107. Half two (terminalize-the-ambiguous) is not statically gateable at all. Nothing in the AST distinguishes a Stripe timeout from a Stripe rejection — that is a property of the SDK's error taxonomy at runtime — so no lint can fail on coachflow#1 refunds.service, the P1 that motivates the class. The proposed catch-annotation lint ('rethrow, or write a row selected by a named sweep query, or carry // AMBIGUOUS-SAFE') is honest as a declaration gate and does fail on the connect-webhook swallow, but note its second clause is not statically determinable, so in practice it degrades to 'rethrow or annotate' and the annotation is the escape hatch that makes it toothless on the timeout case. The fault-injection harness is the only thing that can go red on the refund double-spend, and like verify-probe-sensitivity.mjs it depends on a hand-authored failure taxonomy per provider — which is fine, but it is a test suite with a completeness registry, not a lint.
verdicts.replacement: Split into (1) `partial-multi-store-write-with-no-compensation` — executable-strong, keep the tx-client-purity AST lint, the outside-array-mutation lint, the artifact-before-write compensating-delete requirement, and the `set -e`/trap shell rule. (2) `ambiguous-failure-recorded-as-definite` — honest feasibility executable-partial. Its only failable gate is a provider fault-injection harness with a REGISTRY: every module calling a mutating provider method must appear in `provider-fault-coverage.json` naming the three injections it replays ({terminal-rejection, timeout-after-success, timeout-before-send}), each asserting 'provider effect count === 1' after replay to completion; an unregistered mutating call site fails the build. The static part of it asserts only that every `catch` around a provider mutation branches on a classifier function (an identifier from a declared error-taxonomy module) rather than on a bare string/instanceof — that IS mechanical and would have failed on refunds.service.

verdicts.argument: The only gate claim in the set with a working implementation already on disk: verify-probe-sensitivity.mjs applies decoy mutations to a scratch copy and requires the probe to exit non-zero, which is the correct inversion — the probe must be demonstrated red before it is trusted. The other pieces survive attack individually. Stryker scoped to PR-changed files genuinely goes red on luxebook#108: because the expectation and the implementation call the same formatter, mutating the formatter changes both sides and the test still passes, which is by definition a surviving mutant. 'Test files may not import the formatter/derivation under test' is a mechanical import lint that fails on the same exemplar independently. Computing an E2E workflow's transitive import graph and requiring every file in it to be covered by `pull_request.paths` is deterministic and fails on luxebook#67 (tenant-resolution.middleware.ts). The skip-instead-of-fail half is already shipped and proven in verify-skip-policy.mjs. Two honest residuals worth stating rather than hiding: the negative-fixture matrix only proves the probe catches failures somebody imagined — 403-for-all had to occur to a human before it became a fixture, and the luxebook#107 cf-mitigated defect recurred three rounds precisely because nobody imagined it; and '`|| true` wrapping any command whose status is later used as health evidence' needs dataflow, so it must be narrowed to 'no `|| true` anywhere inside a step whose id/name is registered as a verification step'. Neither residual undermines the executable-strong label, because unlike every other gate here this one fails closed on the absence of the artifact.

Mostly earns its label, but one sub-shape — the one carrying the most P1s — is undecidable and is being sold as covered. Rule (b), 'for every model carrying tenantId in schema.prisma, fail any update/updateMany/delete whose where lacks tenantId', is schema-derived rather than memory-derived, mechanical, and fails on luxebook#110 exactly. Rule (d) is the sharpest idea in the taxonomy: mechanically compare the key-set of a sweep's selection `where` against the key-set of its CAS `where` and fail on any column present in the first and absent in the second — that goes red on luxebook#1 reminder-scheduler and stays green after the fix (caveat: only when both are inline object literals; spread/builder forms need a lint banning them in sweep files, which should be stated as part of the gate). Rule (a) is real ts-morph scope analysis but noisy — reading an entity to authorize and then using its id is the normal case, so the annotated-exemption carries most of the load and will be applied reflexively. The failure is the serializable-SSI sub-shape. coachflow#3 (grant inserts credit rows, cancellation updates the booking, one-way rw-dependency, no cycle, both commit) cannot be detected by any static rule: deciding whether two transactions can form a dangerous structure requires their full read/write sets and the concurrent schedule. Claiming executable-strong over a class whose flagship P1 mechanism is formally undecidable is the same overreach the class itself indicts.
verdicts.replacement: Keep (b)(c)(d) at executable-strong, with (d) paired to a lint banning non-literal where-clauses in sweep/executor directories so the key-set comparison cannot be evaded. Demote (a) to a review prompt. For the SSI sub-shape, the honest partial is a read/write-set declaration gate rather than a detector: any `$transaction` opened with isolationLevel Serializable must declare, in a sibling comment or a registry entry, the tables it reads-but-does-not-write; the gate computes those sets from the callback's prisma calls, compares them to the declaration, and FAILS whenever the read-set is not a subset of the write-set unless the site also contains an explicit `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`, a sentinel write to the read table, or an annotated exemption naming the conflicting transaction. That asserts only what is mechanically true — 'you are relying on SSI to protect a table you only read' — and it would have gone red on coachflow#3 without pretending to reason about cycles.

verdicts.argument: The executable-partial label is honestly chosen and the Playwright multi-context suite is the right instrument, but two of the four lints are mis-specified in opposite directions. '`any if (guard) followed by await must re-check guard before its terminal write`' fires on essentially every async function in a NestJS codebase — it is a pattern-match with no notion of what a guard is, will be suppressed wholesale within days, and is a textbook grep-that-matches-the-wrong-thing. Conversely, the cookie-attribute rule is UNDERSOLD as part of a partial: 'the logout Set-Cookie attribute set equals the set attribute set except expiry' is fully mechanical both statically (compare the options object literal at `res.cookie(NAME, …)` with the one at `res.clearCookie(NAME, …)` for the same name constant) and at runtime (one integration test hitting login then logout), and it fails on luxebook#78 precisely, where clearCookie passed only `{ path }`. That deserves to be broken out as an executable-strong sub-gate rather than buried. 'Ban `fetch(` outside each app's lib/api/http.ts' is cheap, mechanical, and directly addresses the cross-app-parity exemplar. The genuinely partial core — which carrier wins, cross-tab propagation, already-mounted component state — is only reachable by the interleaving suite, and that suite's interleavings are hand-enumerated, so the class should say so rather than imply the matrix is derived.
verdicts.replacement: Drop the `if (guard) … await` lint. Promote to executable-strong, as its own check: (i) cookie attribute symmetry — static comparison of the res.cookie/res.clearCookie option literals per cookie-name constant, plus a runtime assertion on the two Set-Cookie headers; (ii) `fetch(` banned outside lib/api/http.ts per app; (iii) a shared cross-app conformance suite (send-credentials, refresh-and-retry on 401, logout calls the API) that BOTH apps must import — the gate being that each app's package must list the conformance suite in its test entry points, so a sibling app that reimplements the protocol cannot silently opt out. Leave the carrier-precedence core at executable-partial with an explicit registry: `session-carriers.json` naming every writer of identity (cookie probe, explicit sign-in, OAuth callback, guest migration) — a new writer not listed fails the build, and each listed writer must appear in the interleaving matrix. That converts 'we thought of these interleavings' into 'every writer is covered', which is the only mechanical part available.

verdicts.argument: Survives attack better than any other correctness class, because its gates assert structure in the storage layer rather than intent in the code. 'Any prisma.create for a model on a declared IDEMPOTENT_MODELS list must be an upsert or be backed by a @@unique on the natural key in schema.prisma' is decidable from two files, goes red on coachflow#1 (MakeupCredit created afresh per grantedForBookingId), goes green on the fix, and it is registry-shaped so a new model that should be idempotent fails until classified — exactly the pattern verify-mutation-claim-registry.mjs already proves in this corpus. 'Flag redis.get(k) followed by del(k)|set(k) in the same function without Lua/GETDEL' is a local AST pattern that fails on luxebook#85's double password reset and cannot be satisfied by a decoy elsewhere in the file. The idempotency-key rule needs one restatement to be honest — 'read from a persisted DB column' is provenance analysis nobody will implement, but the decidable form ('the idempotencyKey argument must be an identifier or property access, never a call to randomUUID/Date.now/uuid and never a template literal containing one') still fails on coachflow#1 refunds. The one sub-rule that must be replaced rather than kept is 'flag two different key-builder expressions producing a lock key for the same resource type': nothing tells a checker that two expressions denote the same resource. The workable form is to make it impossible instead of detectable — all redis lock calls must take their key from a single exported keys module with one exported function per resource type, lint-enforced, which collapses luxebook#105's createHold/reschedule divergence into a single visible site. The double-fire CI harness is real but payload synthesis is the human part; it is backing, not the gate.

The executable-partial label is right, but it is applied uniformly across sub-shapes with wildly different feasibility, which hides one strong gate and one bad grep. Strong and mislabelled as partial: 'run the provisioning script twice in CI with a different token and assert no file under /etc/systemd/system/*.d/ contains the first token' is deterministic, container-runnable, needs no third-party access, and goes red on luxebook#107's surviving 10-metrics.conf drop-in — that is executable-strong and should be stated as such. Bad grep: the migration rule keys on column names matching /\*Normalized|\*Hash|\*E164/, which is an inventory drawn from memory — the exact anti-pattern the class describes — and misses a canonicalization column named `canonicalPhone` or `phoneKey`. Genuinely partial and correctly labelled: anything requiring `stripe webhook_endpoints list`, `vercel env ls`, or OAuth redirect URIs, since those need live credentials, are unavailable on fork PRs, and are the entries the class itself says are most reliably forgotten — a repo-scoped gate cannot reach them by construction, and that limit should be stated as a property of the class rather than as a config detail.
verdicts.replacement: Restate as three tiers. Tier A executable-strong: the idempotent-rerun harness (run provisioning twice with rotated credentials; assert exit 0 both times and that no artifact under the config drop-in directories contains the first credential; kill run one midway and assert run three converges). Tier B executable-strong with the naming grep replaced: any migration that adds a column must either contain a backfill UPDATE for that column, or carry a `-- NO-BACKFILL: reason` marker, whenever ts-morph finds that column used in a `where` anywhere at the current SHA — derived from the schema and the code rather than from a name regex, so it fires on luxebook#78/#83 and on the next canonicalization column whatever it is called. Add the checked-in legacy fixture dataset as a required E2E input. Tier C explicitly NOT gateable in-repo: externally-owned registrations. The honest artifact there is a generated cutover checklist — the preflight script emits the step list from a repo-wide grep of the OLD value, and the gate asserts only that the runbook's step list is byte-identical to the generated output (i.e. that nobody hand-edited it), which is mechanical and is the only claim a repo-scoped check can license.

verdicts.argument: Three of the gate pieces are best-in-class and one is a repo-wide grep that will be turned off in a week. Best-in-class: 'a property decorated @IsOptional() whose TS type excludes | null must carry a null-rejecting decorator' is a two-node AST check, precise, near-zero false positives, and it fails on coachflow#1 compliance (expiresAt:null → new Date(null) → 1970) and passes on the fix; 'ban new Date(expr) where expr's type includes null' is free from the type checker; and 'ban `as T` on a res.json() result outside a schema-parsing module' is not a proposal at all — it is already implemented and proven as verify-trust-boundary-decoding.mjs in this corpus. The Nest-metadata contract fuzz (send explicit null to every optional field, assert 400, never 500, never 2xx-with-mutation) is real because route enumeration is derivable from decorators rather than from a list. The failure is 'assert each numeric limit literal (upload size, min-notice hours) appears exactly once in the repo': there is no way to distinguish the magic 5 that is a featured-services cap from the 5 that is a retry count, so this fires on hundreds of innocent literals and is a grep matching the wrong thing at industrial scale. The TSX date-comparison lint is salvageable but must derive its field-name regex from schema.prisma rather than from a hand-typed /expiresAt|startsAt|regClosesAt/ — otherwise the next authoritative date field silently escapes, which is the class's own mechanism reproduced in its gate.
verdicts.replacement: Keep the @IsOptional/null, new Date(null), res.json-cast, and Nest-metadata fuzz gates at executable-strong. Replace the numeric-literal-uniqueness rule with a narrow registry: a `limits.ts` exporting one named const per domain limit, plus a lint that the arguments of a declared set of limit-consuming call sites (@MaxFileSize, min-notice comparisons, the multipart config) must be identifiers imported from it — failable, low-noise, and it makes the client/server pair derive from one value. Generate the date-field regex for the TSX lint from schema.prisma's DateTime columns. State the Playwright 'enabled button ⇒ 2xx' matrix as backing rather than gate: it is only as complete as the seeded states, so it needs the same state-inventory registry as the reachable-state class.

verdicts.argument: Highest-value class in the set — recurrence 25, existing_rule 'none', and unlike most of the others its gates are local, syntactic, and go red on the exact cited lines. 'Flag any findFirst/findMany whose where contains only a parent FK and whose orderBy is createdAt desc, inside refunds/*, *webhook*, notification*, *sweep*' is two AST predicates plus a directory scope; it fails on coachflow#1 refunds picking the newest refundable Payment and on the package-email balance re-derivation, and the `// ANCHORED:` suppression naming the persisted anchor column is the honest escape hatch rather than a loophole, because the named column must exist in schema.prisma. 'Any provider call carrying a stripeAccount option must source it from the loaded record row, never business.stripeAccountId, outside the onboarding module' is a property-name ban — normally a smell, but legitimate here because the banned property IS the wrong authority, so matching the name is matching the defect, not a proxy for it. Same for banning `offering.config.*` reads inside fulfilment/issuance/ledger paths, and for requiring every query over a model's ledger children to include a declared activation-boundary column. One piece needs a caveat rather than a rewrite: 'a type-level test asserting the snapshot's keys are a superset of the config keys fulfilment uses' is not achievable while config is a Prisma `Json` column, since neither side has keys at the type level — the workable form is to require a typed PurchaseSnapshot and forbid `Json` for the offering config, which is a schema change, not a gate. The create→cancel(pending intent)→reactivate→pay→execute contract test is the rare backing suite whose fixture is fully specified by the class itself.

Two halves with opposite feasibility are averaged into one 'partial', which hides a strong gate behind a weak one. The framework-composition half is deterministic and should be executable-strong: a route-topology test against the BUILT apps, asserting every client-declared target resolves to the intended handler, goes red on luxebook#94 (/admin/admin/posthog from basePath double-prepending) and on luxebook#86 (vercel.json rewrites vs middleware order) because it observes the built router rather than reading the config; banning localStorage/new Date()/getToken() in the render body of server-rendered components is a plain AST rule; `prisma validate` over fenced blocks in docs/**/*.md is trivially real; and the TZ=Pacific/Kiritimati frozen-clock hydration test is a fixture, not a judgement call. The vendor-semantics half is genuinely weak and the proposed gate is theater: 'require a recorded SDK/spec probe artifact for every third-party field newly branched on' fails closed on absence, which has some value, but the artifact is satisfied by pasting a docs URL — it asserts that someone typed something, not that the semantics are right. Nothing can fail on coachflow#3's window.open-returns-null-on-success, because the .d.ts says `Window | null` and both readings type-check; nothing can fail on the unexpanded Charge.refunds, because `expand` semantics are absent from the types entirely. The one mechanical vendor rule that survives is the pagination one ('accessing .data on a provider type that also declares has_more, outside the paginating gateway'), and it survives precisely because the vendor's own type carries the tell.
verdicts.replacement: Split into (1) `framework-composition-order-assumed` — executable-strong: route-topology test against built apps for every declared client target; render-body bans in server components; prisma validate over doc fences; hydration test under a hostile TZ and frozen clock. (2) `vendor-value-semantics-assumed` — honest feasibility executable-partial, and its gate must be fixture replay, not paperwork: a checked-in vendor-fixture corpus (unexpanded charge, $0 trial invoice, post-deauthorization event, truncated refund page, duplicate and reverse-order deliveries) that every handler must be replayed against, with a registry requiring each vendor-event type the app subscribes to to have at least one adversarial fixture — an unfixtured event type fails the build. Keep the has_more AST rule and the monotonicMax() requirement on webhook-written timestamp columns; drop the probe-artifact requirement to an implementer_question, since it licenses no assertion.

verdicts.argument: The gate is bound to the wire rather than to the config, which is the property the rest of the taxonomy keeps failing to achieve. 'Boot the app under a Playwright route handler, visit a route seeded with a canary, force an error, assert the canary appears in ZERO outbound bodies to any telemetry host' cannot be satisfied by the tested path alone — it observes replay uploads, autocapture, and breadcrumbs because it observes every request, which is exactly why it catches the surfaces the hand-written denylist forgot (coachflow#13's replay URL capture, the PostHog autocapture text). That is the honest inversion the class demands and it goes red on the cited exemplars. The property-based canary-at-every-leaf test with 'newly added schema field fails by default until allowlisted' is a completeness gate in the proven shape; its only caveat, worth stating in the class, is that it presupposes the vendor publishes a machine-readable event schema — true for Sentry, not for PostHog, where the leaf set must be maintained from the SDK's own payload types instead. 'Enabling a replay/recording config key requires a sibling redaction-callback key in the same options object' is a local AST check on an options literal and fails on coachflow#13's missing maskCapturedNetworkRequestFn. The value-based logger middleware that regex-scans serialized output for email/JWT/PAN shapes and throws in CI goes red on the email-transport `message.to` exemplar, which the key-based scrubber structurally could not see. And the no-JS form half is not a proposal — verify-form-degradation.mjs already exists and is proven against channel#6.

The load-bearing gate is written and proven: verify-pipeline-causality.mjs parses the workflow DAG and requires each deploy job to run the proof steps itself, or `needs:` a job that does, or be triggered by workflow_run on the proving workflow with a conclusion guard — which fails on channel#7 and coachflow#10 by construction, since correlation and causation are distinguishable in the parsed graph. Several siblings are equally mechanical and some are off-the-shelf: banning `${{ inputs.* }}` and `${{ github.event.* }}` inside `run:` bodies is a syntactic check that goes red on luxebook#86's command-injection SSH script; requiring `fingerprint:` on ssh/scp actions is a key-presence check; requiring a preflight asserting every reachable secret is non-empty before the first step referencing secrets.* is an ordering check over a per-job secret set; and diffing `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_*` reads against turbo.json `env` plus Dockerfile ARG/ENV plus compose build args is set asymmetry over four parseable files. Two pieces need honest restatement rather than removal: 'a job annotated `# required-invariant: true` may not be reachable only via a job containing an external network probe' depends on an annotation nobody is forced to add unless migrations jobs are enumerated from the migration directory, and detecting 'external network probe' by regexing curl/dig is a wrong-match risk; and 'post-job, grep the run log for known credential prefixes' misses opaque credentials like cloudflared tokens, so the reliable form is the narrower one already listed — no `echo`/`printf` of any variable assigned from `systemctl cat|show`, which is what actually leaked NEWEXEC in luxebook#107.

Half the gate works and half rests on axe-core doing something axe-core does not do. What works: the form-adapter half is exhaustively enumerable from packages/ui/src/index.ts, so 'every export of components/form rendered inside useForm({ disabled: true }) must be disabled AND absent from submitted values; setFocus(name) must focus it; every generated helper/error id must appear in the control's aria-describedby' is a completeness gate over a derived list, and it goes red on luxebook#71 for form-input, textarea, select, toggle and chip-group simultaneously — which is the right blast radius, since the class's own complaint is per-component fixing. The `outline-none` without focus-visible lint and the ban on literal strings in aria-* props inside packages/ui are trivially mechanical. What does not work: 'run axe-core on every state of the machine' cannot fail on this class's own flagship exemplars. axe does not detect that focus fell to document.body after a subtree swap, and it does not detect that a live region was mounted already populated — both are temporal properties of a transition, not static properties of a tree, and both are the exact luxebook#109 defects. Nor is there any mechanism that knows which components 'have an async state machine' and therefore owe the shared helper; without that, the requirement is unenforceable and the second component in the same PR reoccurs exactly as it did.
verdicts.replacement: Keep executable-strong for the packages/ui half, restated as a fixture-registry gate: every export of packages/ui/src/components/form must have an entry in `form-adapter-fixtures.ts` supplying its required props — an unregistered export fails the build — and the generic contract suite runs the disabled/setFocus/aria-describedby assertions over the registry. For the transition half, honest feasibility is executable-partial and the honest assertion is: every component that both calls a data hook and renders three or more branches must be listed in `async-phase-components.json`, and each listed component must have a test invoking the shared helpers assertFocusRetainedAcrossTransition() and assertLiveRegionMountedEmpty() — the gate checks list membership and helper invocation, which is mechanical, and the helpers (not axe) carry the actual assertions. State plainly that axe-core covers neither exemplar; it is additive coverage for static violations only.

verdicts.argument: This is `verification-bound-to-a-proxy-not-to-the-behavior` in the medium of prose, and that class's own merge rationale already says deploy gates, unit tests and path filters 'differ only in medium'. A document line reading 'the tenant rule is proven for all backend ops' is an assertion bound to something adjacent to the claim, produced by an actor who wanted a green signal, and structurally incapable of going red — the identical mechanism and the identical asymmetric failure mode. The proposed gate confirms the merge by reproducing the parent class's defect: requiring `<!-- verified: path:line@sha -->` and checking that ripgrep finds the named symbol at that path asserts that a symbol EXISTS, not that it ENFORCES the claim. An anchor pointing at CustomerService.ts would satisfy the gate while luxebook#105's README claim stays false, because the defect there is a bare `where: { id }` inside the very file the anchor names. A gate that is satisfied by a token occurring near the right place, while the property it claims is violated, is precisely the channel#6 probe defect — self-refuting by the taxonomy's own criterion. The two genuinely strong pieces (type-checking assertions generated from the doc's own code fences, which fails on acquireLock declared as Promise<boolean> vs the documented owner-token contract; and `prisma validate` over fenced Prisma blocks) are both instances of the parent class's principle — bind the assertion to the artifact under test — and belong there. Counter-argument worth recording: the consumers differ (CI reads test results, humans and agents read prose), so if the taxonomy is organized by who is deceived rather than by mechanism, keep it separate.
verdicts.replacement: Fold into `verification-bound-to-a-proxy-not-to-the-behavior` as its prose medium, and replace the anchor gate with the parent class's rule applied to documents: a maturity claim ('proven', 'enforced', 'fixed in PR #N', 'always') must carry `<!-- verified-by: <test-id> -->`, and the gate asserts the test id exists in the suite, is not skipped (reusing verify-skip-policy.mjs), and passed at this SHA. That binds the doc claim to a behavior assertion instead of to a file:line, and it decays automatically when the test does — a doc edit can no longer close a finding, because closing it now requires a green named test. Keep the two derived checks (doc-fence signature assertions type-checked against the real module; prisma validate over doc fences) and the one-route-literal-per-operation check, sourcing route literals from a generated manifest.

verdicts.argument: Two problems: the class bundles two different temporal mechanisms, and its most-cited gate is undecidable. On scope — 'not yet settled' (auth in its transient null, a modal seeding from an unresolved query) and 'settled once and never revisited' (a render-time `now` that goes stale, a cached role that the server has since changed) are opposite failures; the first needs a re-run when data arrives, the second needs invalidation or recomputation, and their gates share nothing. On feasibility — 'ban rendering entitlement/permission UI from any value not obtained in the same render pass as the server's authorization response' has no mechanical reading whatsoever: no analysis identifies 'entitlement UI', and 'same render pass' is a runtime property. That sub-rule is unimplementable as stated and should not appear under executable-strong. What genuinely works: 'ban bare new Date()/Date.now() in the render body of list/menu components' is an AST check on call position (inside the JSX-returning body, not inside a hook or callback) and goes red on luxebook#63's canMarkComplete; exhaustive-deps as error with a required justification comment on each suppression is mechanical for the comment half, unenforceable for the 'paired test' half; and the telemetry contract test asserting call ORDER (identify before the first capture, group cleared on tenant change) is writable and fails on the PostHog exemplars — but it is one hand-written suite per provider, not a repo-wide gate, and 'required test pattern for any modal-seeding effect' again presumes a way to identify modal-seeding effects that does not exist without a registry.
verdicts.replacement: Narrow the class to the settling direction ('a decision is made from state that has not settled, and nothing revises it when it does') and move the render-time-`now` and cached-role exemplars to a sibling `authoritative-value-cached-past-its-validity`. Downgrade feasibility to executable-partial, with these honest assertions: (i) the new Date()/Date.now()-in-render-body lint, which stays strong; (ii) exhaustive-deps as error plus a lint that every suppression of it carries a `// SEEDING-JUSTIFIED:` comment naming a test id, with the gate checking the test id resolves — declaration-shaped, and it is the only way to reach the modal-seeding case without a registry; (iii) the telemetry ordering suite, stated as a required per-provider fixture rather than a lint. Replace the unimplementable entitlement rule with a type-level one that IS mechanical: brand the server's authorization response (`Authz<'canMarkComplete'>`) and type permission-gated component props to accept only the branded type, so passing a cached role fails tsc at every call site — that turns an undecidable render-timing question into a compile error.

verdicts.argument: The merge holds — timezone authority and design tokens really are one mechanism (the domain designates an authority, the call site reaches for the ambient or raw equivalent, and neither propagates on a later change) — and, unusually, they also share a gate SHAPE, which is the right test for whether a merge earns its keep: ban the raw API/literal, force the authority-carrying helper. The timezone lint is a textbook honest gate: no-restricted-syntax over date-fns format/startOfDay/endOfDay/parseISO and Date.prototype.getHours/getMinutes/getDay inside scheduling, booking and calendar-UI paths, allowing only date-fns-tz forms, goes red on luxebook#59 and luxebook#79 and green on the fix, with no semantic judgement required. The TZ=UTC vs TZ=Asia/Hong_Kong CI matrix requiring byte-identical results is behavior-bound and would have caught the display-vs-book divergence — with one caveat that belongs in the class text: a suite that mocks the clock or stubs the formatter produces identical output in both timezones and passes vacuously, so the matrix must be paired with the mutation-testing regime from `verification-bound-to-a-proxy` or it is itself a proxy gate. The color/radius/shadow/tracking literal lint is mechanical. Two sub-rules should be dropped rather than kept: 'resolving tracking/weight pairs against values extracted from DESIGN.md' means parsing prose for token values and will break on the first reformatting — the fix is a machine-readable design/tokens.json from which DESIGN.md is generated, and then the comparison is trivial; and 'a CI check that any PR adding a route- or state-level component also references a file under design/' is a proxy satisfied by adding an unused import, exactly the shape this taxonomy exists to reject.

missing_classes: viewport-variant-implemented-twice-with-no-parity-check — the single largest unnamed cluster in the corpus (~33 findings across luxebook and nutribuddy, larger than several named classes): 'Preserve bottom-nav inset until the lg breakpoint', 'Keep tablet widths on the responsive header path', 'Preserve the guest draft when crossing the desktop breakpoint', 'Restore focus to the remounted mobile trigger', 'Keep desktop setup out of the mobile bottom sheet', 'Implement the desktop split surface instead of wrapping mobile UI', 'Use the three-column Saved layout at 1280px', 'Remove the mobile bottom reserve on desktop'. Mechanism: a layout variant is a SECOND IMPLEMENTATION of the same feature, gated by a media query or a width branch, and state, focus, affordances and required fields are carried by only one branch — with both trees sometimes mounted so crossing the breakpoint remounts and drops state. It is not the a11y class (the contract is dropped by a width branch, not by an async swap) and not the design-token class (the values are fine; the branch is the defect). Highly gateable, and notably the taxonomy's nutribuddy coverage is three generic exemplars while this is where nutribuddy's actual review mass sits — evidence the truncation disclosure understates the reconstruction gap. Honest gate: render every route at each declared breakpoint in the Tailwind config and diff the accessible trees for elements present in one and absent in the other unless allowlisted; a resize-crossing test asserting focus target and form state survive; and a lint that any component with two width-branched subtrees must render one shared state container.

sort-key-that-is-not-a-total-order — 'Preserve turn order when timestamps tie', 'Preserve relative order when reordering null-featured items', 'Keep null-featured ordering aligned with backend sort', 'Keep the Saved grid stable during undo', 'Do not key active card responses by request order', 'Enforce event ordering for start rate' (~8 findings, luxebook + nutribuddy). Mechanism: an ORDER BY / comparator whose key set does not uniquely determine a row (ties on timestamp, NULLs in a featuredOrder column, insertion order used as identity), so the tiebreak is delegated to the database planner or the JS engine and two consumers — backend list and frontend reorder — materialize different sequences from the same data. The taxonomy touches it only as a one-clause aside in `boundary-contract-assumed` ('orderings that disagree between screens'), which misattributes it: the two sides can share one predicate and still disagree, because the key is underdetermined. Gate is unusually clean: assert every ORDER BY in list endpoints terminates in a unique column (id) and declares NULLS FIRST/LAST explicitly; property test that shuffling input rows yields byte-identical output.

locale-bundle-key-set-divergence — 'Cover every resolver state in the Chinese locale', 'Localize carousel ARIA labels instead of hardcoding English', 'Translate profile inputs before patching', 'Generalize locale 404 copy beyond salon-missing cases'. Small count but a mechanism the taxonomy names nowhere, and one of the most mechanically gateable defects in the whole corpus: a new string surface lands in one locale bundle and the other falls back silently to the source language, so the failure is invisible to anyone testing in the default locale. Partially overlaps `reachable-state-with-no-exit` (new states shipped without copy) and `a11y-contract-dropped` (hardcoded English aria strings), but neither class's gate would fire. Honest gate: key-set equality across locale bundles as a hard build failure, plus a lint banning literal strings in user-facing props including aria-*, plus a render pass over every state-inventory entry in each locale asserting no untranslated-key fallback.

test-precondition-never-reaches-the-state-under-test — 'Use reachable pre-recipe guest-limit fixtures', 'Use reachable guest-limit states for the quota contract', 'Exhaust the guest follow-up limit before expecting a gate', 'Enter the guest card flow before asserting recipes', 'Drive the desktop stepper from reachable setup state'. Distinct from `verification-bound-to-a-proxy`: the assertion there is bound to the wrong subject, whereas here the assertion is CORRECT but the arrange step never drives the system into the state it names, so the assertion evaluates against the initial state and passes for a reason unrelated to the behavior. It survives mutation testing of production code in some cases (the mutant is never reached), so the parent class's flagship gate does not catch it. Honest gate: every test that names a state must assert the precondition holds immediately before the act step — enforceable as a required `expect(atState(X))` line, or by a coverage assertion that the branch under test was actually executed.

point-fix-applied-to-the-instance-rather-than-the-factory — appears as a symptom inside three classes (luxebook#109's identical focus defect recurring in the second component of the SAME PR; luxebook#71's five form adapters; the round-after-round doc re-flagging) but is never named as a mechanism with its own gate, despite being the strongest explanation for why recurrence counts are as high as they are. Mechanism: a finding is closed by editing the one cited site, and the structural siblings — other members of the same barrel export, other call sites of the same pattern, other components in the same phase family — are neither enumerated nor exempted, so the same defect ships in the same diff.
