The corpus's own `grep-for-siblings` rule is the right idea but fires only on 'security literal removed'. Honest gate: a fix-closure check that, for every file:line cited in a review finding, computes the structural sibling set (same barrel, same AST pattern, same directory role) and fails the fix commit unless each sibling is either changed or listed in a `siblings-exempt` note on the commit.

verdicts.argument:
THE CANONICAL CASE — the diagnosis is wrong in three independently checkable ways, and the true answer is establishable from git.

(1) WRONG RULE CITED. The rule whose content is the missing fix is `concurrency-cas/single-use-token-consumption` (maturity: proven, impact CRITICAL, in the catalog since 2026-05-12), whose ✅ block is literally `updateMany({ where: { id, consumedAt: null }, data: {...} })` + `if (result.count !== 1) lose`. Equally direct is `concurrency-cas/storage-gate-not-js`, whose applies-to reads: 'Any code shaped like `const x = await read(); if (x.flag) throw; await update(x, ...)`' — which is completeUploadAction verbatim (/Users/SeanCai/Desktop/projects/channel/apps/functions/admin/src/handler.ts:1790-1793 `const doc = await get('images', …); if (doc.status !== 'pending') return err('CONFLICT'…)`, then unpredicated `updateDoc('images', imageId, { status: 'active', … })` at :1855). `mint-once-vs-mint-on-demand` is a category error here: its content is 'do not RE-mint a shareable token', unrelated to single-winner claims.

(2) A FACTUAL CLAIM THAT IS FALSE. The taxonomy says storage-gate-not-js is 'loaded from the concurrency-cas category, which the by-phase table marks mandatory only at G4 for diffs already recognised as concurrency work'. `git show HEAD:INDEX.md` line 57: G4 — Implementation lists `concurrency-cas (storage-gate-not-js, race-test-contract, status-set-creep, monetary-decimal-symmetry, cross-tx-cas-recompute)` under **Mandatory**, with no conditional. Every conditional entry in that table carries an explicit '(if …)' — 'time-and-timezone (if scheduling)', 'silent-no-op-integrations (if 3rd-party API)', 'frontend-async-state (if React mutations)'. concurrency-cas at G4 carries none. The rule was unconditionally mandatory at the phase where the code was written.

(3) THE TRIGGER QUESTION, ANSWERED FROM GIT RATHER THAN GUESSED. Yes — the keyword list was missing upload/finalize/complete, and this is provable: the INDEX row `| finalize, complete, activate, settle, claim, publish, or ANY status: A → B that may happen at most once | concurrency-cas/single-use-token-consumption (shape trigger …) |` is an UNCOMMITTED working-tree edit to /Users/SeanCai/.claude/external-mirrors/engineering-craft/INDEX.md dated 2026-08-06 (git status: ' M INDEX.md'; the row appears only in `git diff`). The same diff adds the whole `verification-integrity/` category and the 'Trigger scope — read this before the trigger table' doctrine. At ship time the rule's own `applies-to` was vocabulary-keyed: '`consumedAt`, `usedAt`, `redeemedAt`, `spent`, `claimed`' — and completeUpload spells its one-shot transition as a status enum.

BUT — and this is the part the taxonomy misses — one trigger DID match and routed to the WRONG rule. completeUpload contains `if (doc.status !== 'pending')`, which matches the committed INDEX row '`status !== 'X'`, status enum predicates → **concurrency-cas/status-set-creep-on-state-machine-evolution**'. That rule is about allow-lists vs negation chains and says nothing about atomicity; a reader who followed the table correctly loaded a rule the code passes. A missing row is a miss; a row that routes a matching shape to a rule that blesses it is worse.

(4) 'ONLY CONSULTED FOR NEW CODE?' — NO, and the taxonomy's exemplar sentence is chronologically backwards. `git log -S` on the channel repo: completeUploadAction was introduced in 5a043e0, 2026-06-30 11:13:29 +0800; the OEM `finalizeClaim` CAS was introduced in 871adff LATER THE SAME DAY, prompted by a Codex P1 (the code comment at handler.ts:889 says so: 'placed BEFORE any object download or destructive mutation (Codex `871adff` P1)'). So 'the sibling already had a CAS and this shipped without one' is false at ship time. The family failure is the SECOND event: once 871adff landed the claim at handler.ts:892, nobody carried it 890 lines down to handler.ts:1790 in the same file — the fix was applied to the path under review, not to the family.

(5) 'WAS THE CATALOG NEVER OPENED?' — not determinable from artifacts; do not assert it. What IS determinable is stronger: from 2026-07-07 (channel commits 34117a9/2deca4c) the repo's OWN /Users/SeanCai/Desktop/projects/channel/docs/ENGINEERING_CRAFT.md carried a trigger-index row 'upload intents, `submitProject`/finalize, storage objects, rate caps → Upload Lifecycle & Concurrency' AND the rule 'Cas claim before destructive validation (`f2bf266`, `871adff`) … place the consume-once atomic single-winner claim … BEFORE any storage download or destructive mutation'. A matching project-local trigger plus the exact pattern, and completeUpload still shipped without it through the round-5 hardening pass (0085f46, 2026-07-08) that edited `finalizeClaim` in the same file. After 2026-07-07 the cause is not trigger vocabulary at all: it is that neither catalog is executable and neither is ever re-run against inherited code.

Meanwhile the one row that did match, `status !== \'X\'`, routes to status-set-creep — an allow-list rule the code passes. The family half is a distinct, later failure: the sibling OEM CAS did not exist when completeUpload shipped (5a043e0 11:13 vs 871adff same day, after a Codex P1); when it landed, the fix was applied to the reviewed path only, 890 lines from its twin in the same file. And from 2026-07-07 the repo\'s own docs/ENGINEERING_CRAFT.md carried BOTH a matching trigger row (upload intents / finalize) and the exact CAS-claim rule, and the defect still survived a round-5 hardening pass that edited finalizeClaim in that same file — after that date the cause is not vocabulary but the absence of any executable form and of any re-scan of inherited code.' verdicts.argument:
'existing_rule: none / no rule existed' is false and is the most consequential factual error in the taxonomy. `categories/concurrency-cas/rules/async-event-revalidates-live-pointer.md` (maturity: verified, impact CRITICAL, added 2026-07-11 in 26df6a5) has applies-to: 'Any handler consuming an async completion event for a resource that a MUTABLE local pointer connects to its beneficiary (payment→booking, job→task, upload→record) — where the beneficiary can be re-pointed, re-funded, or re-assigned while the async operation is in flight.' That is this class's mechanism stated in the class's own words. Its historical incident is the CoachFlow one: 'an expired-and-swept card hold's PaymentIntent succeeded late after the seat was re-booked with different funding — the webhook routed on booking status, re-confirmed the re-funded booking, and kept the charge (silent overcharge); 678 unit tests, 7 E2E journeys and every per-unit gate passed over it'. And the committed INDEX carries the trigger row 'async completion event, late webhook, job-completion callback → concurrency-cas/async-event-revalidates-live-pointer'. Rule, matching trigger, and an identical prior incident all existed. Claiming 'none' means the miner did not grep the catalog for the class it was diagnosing.

The REAL gap is a prescription mismatch, which is a better finding than 'no rule': the rule tells the executor to RE-VALIDATE the live pointer at execution time, while several exemplars need the opposite remedy — CAPTURE the subject at intent time (persist the charge id, the stripeAccountId at charge time, a PurchaseSnapshot of the offering config). Re-validation cannot fix 'refunds sent to the tenant's CURRENT stripeAccountId' or 'redemption parses the package offering's CURRENT config', because there is nothing stale to detect — the live read is the bug. The rule also has no model of a row with multiple logical lives (cancel→reactivate reusing Booking.id) or of composite identity compared on one component.
verdicts.replacement: Set existing_rule to 'concurrency-cas/async-event-revalidates-live-pointer (verified, 2026-07-11; INDEX trigger: async completion event / late webhook / job-completion callback)'. Set why_it_did_not_fire to: 'the gate existed and its trigger matched, but it prescribes the wrong half of the remedy — re-validate-at-execution, not anchor-at-intent. Re-validation cannot detect the sub-shapes where the live read IS the defect (current stripeAccountId, current offering config), and the rule has no model of a recycled row with multiple lives or of a composite identity compared on one component. The CoachFlow refunds exemplar is a recurrence of the very incident this rule was mined from, one month later, in the same service file — evidence that a prose rule with a correct trigger does not survive contact with a second code site.'

verdicts.argument: 'trigger keywords too narrow … a plain `format()` in an admin hook and an `rgba()` literal match neither list' is wrong on the timezone half at the rule level. `time-and-timezone/server-local-trap.md` (maturity: PROVEN) has a SHAPE-based applies-to: 'Any code that touches user-visible scheduling: availability, calendar boundaries, reminders, cross-midnight blocks, TIME FORMATTING, date parsing of user input.' A booking-reschedule hook deriving `dateIso` and a slot picker rendering time labels are time formatting for scheduling — squarely inside it. Worse for the diagnosis: two of the rule's six recorded historical incidents ARE this class's exemplars, verbatim — 'getBlocksForDate used server startOfDay/endOfDay while availability used tenant-local bounds; cross-midnight blocks missed; double-booking' (= luxebook#59) and 'admin calendar Date#getHours() returned viewer-local hour; bookings vanished from day view at 23:30 HK' (= luxebook#79 slot labels). The committed INDEX trigger row is '`parseISO`, `startOfDay`, `getHours`, `Date#`, scheduling' — and 'scheduling' is in it. So: proven rule, matching shape-based applies-to, matching trigger keyword, and the identical incident already recorded — and it recurred anyway at new code sites. That is not a trigger-scoping failure; it is a proven rule with no executable form being re-violated, which the rule's own impact-description already predicted ('the same class of bug recurred at 6 different code sites in one production system because no rule said every time op gets an explicit timezone'). The design-drift half (silent-css-class-vacuum, applies-to: non-standard token names, breakpoint stacks, styled native inputs) genuinely does not reach a raw `rgba()` in a new error-state component — that half of the diagnosis stands.
verdicts.replacement: Split the diagnosis by half. Timezone: 'a PROVEN rule with a shape-based applies-to covering time formatting for scheduling, a matching INDEX keyword, and two of this class\'s exemplars already recorded as its own historical incidents — it did not fire because nothing executes it; the TZ=UTC + TZ=Asia/Hong_Kong matrix it recommends was never made a required check.' Design: 'trigger genuinely too narrow — silent-css-class-vacuum is keyed on unknown token names / breakpoint stacks / native input restyling and has no model of a hand-built component inventing a palette value.' Keeping one blended label hides that the two halves need different fixes (execution vs trigger).

The diagnosis says the PostHog identify/reset ordering problem 'never loads the rule'. It loads a DIFFERENT rule that matches it exactly. `observability/analytics-lifecycle-and-containment.md` (maturity: verified) has historical incident #2: 'reset() fired during the auth /me loading window (loading=true, user=null), splitting sessions across every hard refresh' — which is luxebook#94/coachflow#13's exemplar word for word — plus incident #1 (missing reset-on-logout attributing events to the prior user, = the surviving-group-association exemplar) and incident #3 (analytics capture inside a serializable transaction rolling back the business op). For the latched-modal-seed half orphan-promise names the pattern but is keyed on useEffect-with-server-data-dep / A→B→A / fire-and-forget IIFE. The two things NO rule expresses: classifying a caught error as terminal vs ambiguous before terminalizing (timeout-after-success moves money twice), and compensation in shell scripts, where `set -e` is the thing that skips the rollback the script was written to invoke.'

'the gate existed but asserted the wrong thing' is exactly backwards for the probe and skip exemplars. `verification-integrity/probe-must-fail-on-injected-defect.md` and `verification-integrity/skip-is-a-decision-not-a-default.md` are UNTRACKED files (git status '??' on the whole `categories/verification-integrity/` directory) created 2026-08-06 — after this corpus, in response to it. At review time NO rule anywhere required a probe to be demonstrated failing against a broken fixture. The two rules cited — process/post-merge-deploy-verification ('watch the deploy after every merge', applies-to: every merge of any PR that auto-deploys) and e2e-test-resilience/selector-coupling ('any rename of a label, role, copy string, or test-id') — are not about assertion binding at all; citing them manufactures a gate that did not exist.

The closest things that DID exist are cross-file-seams FAILURE_MODES #7 'Mock-based test passes while real interface drifts' and #10 'Test rewritten alongside behavior change (tautology)' — #7 is trigger-keyed ('mock vs extended class' in the INDEX cross-file-seams row), #10 is not keyed at all. #10 is the exact shape of luxebook#108 (expectation computed with the same formatter the implementation uses).

Separately, channel#7 'smoke tests skip instead of fail' is not a rule-failed-to-fire case at all: /Users/SeanCai/Desktop/projects/channel/docs/ENGINEERING_CRAFT.md positively PRESCRIBES it — 'Every destructive/credentialed suite opens with test.skip(!flag || !hasX(), \'Set VAR=… to run\') so absent credentials skip cleanly with an actionable message — never fail, never half-run.' verdicts.replacement: why_it_did_not_fire → 'no rule existed. The two verification-integrity rules that state this class\'s requirement (probes must be shown failing on a decoy defect; a skip is a dated decision, never a default) are untracked files authored 2026-08-06 in response to this corpus. The rules the taxonomy cited govern something else entirely: post-merge-deploy-verification is a habit about watching deploys; selector-coupling is about renames breaking E2E. The only pre-existing coverage was cross-file-seams #7 (mock/real drift, keyword-triggered) and #10 (test rewritten alongside behaviour — not triggered by anything). And for the skip exemplar the situation is inverted: the repo\'s own craft doc mandates test.skip-on-missing-credentials as the standard, so the defect was produced BY an authoritative rule, not missed by one.'

verdicts.argument:

Every `if (booking.status !== \'X\')` in the codebase', and three of its four historical incidents ARE frontend/notification surfaces (a QR card rendered for the wrong statuses; an admin Reschedule menu item shown for IN_PROGRESS while the executor rejects it; reminders fired for PENDING reschedules). So 'it audits which values a GUARD admits… The exits live in sweeps, TSX, and notification templates that the trigger never reaches' is wrong — the rule explicitly names those surfaces, and its 'Reschedule menu item shown but executor rejects' incident is this class's exact shape.

Nothing anywhere requires enumerating reachable-states × exits as a product, so each round closes one cell and the neighbouring cell reappears.'

verdicts.argument:
'rule scoped to NEW code so inherited/adjacent code was never checked' misdescribes both cited rules. status-set-creep's applies-to is 'Every `if (booking.status !== \'X\')` IN THE CODEBASE' — the widest scope statement in the catalog, explicitly not diff-scoped. And grep-for-siblings contains three rules, not one: `api-rename-cross-cut-grep` (verified) applies-to 'Renaming any: function, class, type, interface, ENUM VALUE, env var, route path, CSS class, GraphQL field, Prisma model field' and demands ≥6 separate greps — the taxonomy cites only security-literal-grep and concludes 'only triggers on security literal removed'.

The real mechanism is the gap between stated scope and actual invocation: the rules' scope is the codebase, but they are only ever LOADED by an INDEX row that matches text in the diff (`status !== 'X'`, 'security literal change', 'rename'). A diff that ADDS an enum member and one writer contains no negation predicate, no rename, and no security literal — so nothing loads a rule whose own applies-to would have covered it. Neither rule has an executable form, so 'scope = whole codebase' is an aspiration no artifact enforces. That is precisely the failure the catalog itself named on 2026-08-06 in the uncommitted INDEX doctrine ('Scope is the FAMILY, not the diff. A twin is by definition not in the diff') and in the new exhaustive-registry rule — evidence the corrected diagnosis is the accepted one.
verdicts.replacement: why_it_did_not_fire → 'scope was stated as the whole codebase and enforced only against the diff. status-set-creep applies to \'every if (booking.status !== X) in the codebase\' and api-rename-cross-cut-grep applies to renaming any enum value, so the content and the stated scope both covered these findings. But every path into those rules runs through an INDEX keyword row that matches text present IN the diff, and a diff that adds an enum member plus one writer contains no negation predicate, no rename and no security literal. With no executable form, whole-codebase scope is unenforceable prose — the exact failure the catalog conceded on 2026-08-06 when it added the \'scope is the FAMILY, not the diff\' doctrine.'

verdicts.argument:
The payload-shape-drift half is verified correct: its applies-to is 'Every form submit; every API client function; every regex/format tightening on an existing DTO field' — request-direction only, exactly as claimed. But the class merges three sub-shapes with three different causes and gives them one label.
• `await res.json() as T`: the rule that governs it, `verification-integrity/parse-dont-cast-at-trust-boundaries`, is an UNTRACKED file created 2026-08-06. At review time no rule existed — not 'trigger too narrow'.
• SDK verb chosen from memory (channel#6 PUT-vs-POST): cross-file-seams FAILURE_MODES #3 'SDK option name unverified against installed type defs' existed and its INDEX trigger row explicitly names 'SDK option name'; and /dev-pipeline:verify-sdk-surface is an auto-invoked executable gate whose stated scope is 'the exact signature and return shape' from the installed .d.ts. So a gate existed and ran; it binds to the method's existence and signature, not to which verb the contract requires.
• @IsOptional() null semantics reaching `new Date(null)`: genuinely unnamed anywhere in the catalog.
One label cannot be right for all three.
verdicts.replacement: why_it_did_not_fire → 'three sub-shapes, three different causes. (1) Client-side eligibility predicates diverging from server guards: payload-shape-drift is keyed on the request direction only (form-state spread, regex tightening) and has no model of an affordance computed independently of the guard. (2) `res.json() as T`: NO rule existed — parse-dont-cast-at-trust-boundaries was authored 2026-08-06 in response to this corpus. And @IsOptional()\'s null-passthrough into a non-nullable sink is named nowhere at all.'

verdicts.argument:
The first half is verified: four-consumer-rule's applies-to is 'Any time you add, rename, change validation of, or delete an env var' and the whole config-drift README enumerates its consumers as env.schema.ts / deploy.yml / .env.example / docs / GitHub Secrets — environment variables only. Volume keys, image tags, cookie Domain and CORS origins are outside it. What is wrong is the implied conclusion that nothing covered the infrastructure exemplars. The deploy-delivery category (13 rules, committed 2026-08-01) is trigger-keyed on '`docker compose up`, `docker save`, `workflow_run`, GHCR/registry pull' and contains `deploy-touches-only-owned-services` (compose config-hash recreation), `explicit-prune-for-tagged-images` and `runner-brokered-artifact-transport` — directly adjacent to the coachflow#7 volume-key and coachflow#2 sha-tag exemplars, though none of them states the resolve-both-files-and-diff requirement. verdicts.replacement: why_it_did_not_fire → 'correct for env vars, incomplete for infrastructure. four-consumer-rule is verifiably env-var-scoped (its applies-to and the config-drift README enumerate env.schema/deploy.yml/.env.example/docs/GitHub Secrets), so volume keys, image tags, bind sources, cookie Domain and CORS origins match no trigger — and where it does fire it counts HOW MANY consumers read a name, never whether producer and consumer resolve it through the same machinery (shell env vs compose interpolation vs @secret vs build ARG). But a deploy-delivery category keyed on `docker compose`/registry pull has existed since 2026-08-01 and covers adjacent ground (compose config-hash recreation, tagged-image prune) without ever requiring two resolutions of the same name to be compared — and several exemplars predate that category, which was mined from them.'

verdicts.argument:

verdicts.argument:
Half right, half wrong, and it omits the most damning evidence.
• WRONG at the rule level: cross-tx-cas-recompute-inside-tx's applies-to is shape-based, not keyword-based — 'Any service method that READS A ROW OUTSIDE `executeInSerializableTransaction`, derives state, then writes inside the tx.' Only the INDEX row is keyed on `tx.commit`/`executeInSerializableTransaction`/multi-service mutation.
• OMITTED: the class's first exemplar is already IN that rule as a recorded incident — 'CoachFlow makeup-grant re-read booking status IN-TX but only INSERTed credit/ledger (never wrote the booking row); SSI had a one-way rw-dependency, no cycle, so it did NOT abort the racing cancel — double compensation. Fixed with SELECT … FOR UPDATE on the booking row (round-16)' — mined into the rule on 2026-07-14 (commit ff4c58a, 'sharpen cross-tx recompute rule — in-tx READ ≠ SSI abort for insert-only tx'). Listing an incident that a proven rule was authored FROM as an example of that rule failing to fire, without saying so, inverts the evidence. (It also means the recurrence count for this class needs date-scoping against already-closed findings.)
• RIGHT: the multi-tenant-fail-closed half is verified — its applies-to is 'Any user lookup by identifier in a multi-tenant schema where the identifier is NOT globally unique', i.e. ambiguous READS; a tenant-scoped findFirst followed by an id-only WRITE matches neither half. And the no-transaction-anywhere sub-shape (read, then plain `update({where:{id}})`) is genuinely outside cross-tx-cas-recompute, which presumes a transaction exists.

What does not reach: (a) the INDEX row is keyed on tx.commit/executeInSerializableTransaction, so a handler with no transaction keyword anywhere — read, then plain update({where:{id}}) — is never routed to it, and the rule itself presumes a tx exists; (b) multi-tenant-fail-closed is about ambiguous READS by non-unique identifier, so a tenant-scoped read followed by an id-only WRITE matches neither half of its trigger. verdicts.argument:
'the rule is keyed on `aria-describedby` and tooltip position math, so it fires for tooltips and popovers ONLY' overstates it. aria-lockstep-and-viewport-clamp's applies-to is 'Any tooltip, popover, MODAL, or DROPDOWN with aria-describedby / aria-controls. Any component positioned with left/right math.' That distinction matters: the fix for scope-too-narrow (widen the trigger) is different from the fix for content-too-thin (write the missing content).

The form-adapter half is correctly diagnosed as uncovered — nothing in the catalog models a wrapper forwarding only the props it was authored for and dropping `field.disabled`/`field.ref`, or generating ids that the focusable element never references. (The nearest, cross-file-seams #6 'Wrapper drops inner lifecycle', is about Observable/Promise/iterator lifecycles, not prop contracts.) Also worth naming in the diagnosis: luxebook#109's identical focus-after-retry defect reappearing in a second component of the SAME PR is not a trigger failure at all — it is a fix applied per-component instead of to a shared phase wrapper, i.e. the family mechanism.
verdicts.replacement: why_it_did_not_fire → 'the trigger is narrower than the class but wider than stated — the rule\'s applies-to explicitly covers modals and dropdowns, so the dialog-without-focus-trap exemplar is in scope; the rule simply contains no model of focus restoration after a subtree swap, live-region mount timing, or focus trapping (its content is describedby lockstep and viewport clamping). And the same-PR recurrence in a second component is the family mechanism, not a trigger gap: the fix was applied per-component rather than to the shared phase wrapper.'

verdicts.argument:
The SDK half is broadly fair — /dev-pipeline:verify-sdk-surface's own description confirms it proves the method exists in the installed .d.ts with 'the exact signature and return shape', which cannot express null-on-success, absent-unless-expanded, or truncated-unless-paged (nuance: it does check the declared return SHAPE, so 'existence only' understates it slightly).

Vendor VALUE semantics: the gate existed and asserted the wrong thing — verify-sdk-surface proves a method exists in the installed .d.ts with the declared signature and return shape, which every one of these calls satisfied, and says nothing about null-on-success, absent-unless-expanded, truncated-unless-paged, or at-least-once unordered delivery; silent-no-op-integrations is scoped to the missing-API-key no-op. Framework COMPOSITION: the opposite failure — cross-file-seams entry #1 is literally \'Framework-prefix doubling\' and the INDEX trigger row names `basePath` verbatim, so a documented mode with a matching keyword recurred anyway. That is non-execution of a prose catalog, not a missing trigger.'

verdicts.argument:
The diagnosis of knowledge-management is verified correct — skill-as-knowledge-base's applies-to is 'Anytime you\'re maintaining engineering-craft ITSELF', so it governs the skill's own lifecycle and not project docs, and nothing binds a doc claim to a file:line at the current SHA.

But the class is under-evidenced where the strongest evidence is sitting in the corpus. /Users/SeanCai/Desktop/projects/channel/docs/ENGINEERING_CRAFT.md documents, as a repo rule with commit citations, 'Cas claim before destructive validation (f2bf266, 871adff): In an upload finalize saga, place the consume-once atomic single-winner claim … BEFORE any storage download or destructive mutation' — while `completeUploadAction` in that same repo (apps/functions/admin/src/handler.ts:1780) has no claim at all. The doc states a scoped observation of ONE path as a general rule, and the review that found completeUpload is the proof nothing re-validates it. The canonical test case for the whole taxonomy is simultaneously an instance of THIS class, and saying so is worth more than any of the current exemplars.

Secondary evidence from the catalog under review: the 2026-08-06 INDEX edit claims 'cross-file-seams ⟳ | 13' while categories/cross-file-seams/FAILURE_MODES.md still indexes 10 entries — the same defect, introduced today, in the artifact that documents the defect.
verdicts.replacement: Keep the diagnosis and add the self-referential exemplars: 'channel docs/ENGINEERING_CRAFT.md documents the CAS-claim-before-destructive-validation rule with commit citations while completeUploadAction in the same repo has no claim — the doc generalised a single path into a repo rule and nothing re-validated it' and 'the craft INDEX asserts cross-file-seams has 13 rules while FAILURE_MODES.md indexes 10'. Sharpen the why to: 'no gate binds a doc claim to a file:line at the current SHA, and knowledge-management governs only the skill\'s own lifecycle — so editing prose is the cheapest way to close a finding, and the artifact that records the lesson is itself unverified.'

verdicts.argument:
The redaction diagnosis is fair and matches the rule: pii-scrubbing-defense-in-depth's applies-to enumerates surfaces from memory — 'anywhere user input or customer records can end up in an exception message, a breadcrumb, a request header, or a query string' — which is precisely the hand-enumeration the class criticises, and its incident ('a cross-file review found 3 telemetry event surfaces … with no test covering them') shows reviewers reading a shared immutable scrubber as compliant. Keep that.

But channel#6's no-JS form GET does not belong in this class. Its mechanism is not 'the scrubber is narrower than the egress surface' — there is no scrubber on that path and no telemetry vendor involved. It is 'the platform's default behaviour when your script does not run': a `<form>` with no `method` natively submits GET, so the browser, not your code, chooses the channel. The craft catalog itself reached the same conclusion on 2026-08-06 by creating a SEPARATE category for it (categories/progressive-degradation/rules/form-without-method-submits-get.md, untracked, with its own INDEX trigger row '`<form` with no `method`, `noscript`, hydration, `client:load`, SSR\'d form markup'). Merging it into the redaction class attaches the wrong gate (canary-through-the-vendor-schema) to a defect fixed by declaring method=POST and by rendering every form with JS disabled.
verdicts.replacement: Split off channel#6 into a new class: 'platform-default-fills-the-gap-when-your-code-does-not-run' — mechanism: a surface's behaviour in the state where the script has not executed (no-JS form submission, SSR-vs-hydration divergence, disabled-JS fallbacks) is chosen by the browser/framework default rather than declared, so the un-run state is never named or tested; existing_rule at review time: none (progressive-degradation was created 2026-08-06); gate: render every form with JS disabled in CI and assert method=POST on any form carrying user data, plus an SSR/no-script snapshot per route. Keep the remaining redaction class as written.

verdicts.argument: Verified end to end and the only diagnosis in the taxonomy I could not fault. checklists/auth-otp-feature.md is a file you must choose to open (it is reachable from the INDEX row '`forgot-password`, `reset-password`, `otp`, `jwt`, `session`, `tokenVersion` → concurrency-cas + enumeration-safety + auth-otp checklist', so the keyword `session` DOES route to it — but routing to a checklist is not a gate). Reading it confirms the second and load-bearing half of the diagnosis: every section is server-side token mechanics — storage-layer CAS on consume, tokenVersion predicate on the user-row write, sibling-credential revocation, status/timing parity, HMAC-at-rest, findMany-fail-closed. There is no model of multiple browser-side carriers, cross-tab propagation, carrier precedence, or already-mounted component state, so a reader who opened it would indeed find nothing that fires. Two refinements worth folding in without changing the verdict: (a) `frontend-async-state/web-storage-is-fallible` covers sessionStorage but for a different failure (access throwing in webviews), so it is adjacent and still silent here; (b) the claim 'nothing forces you to open it' should be stated as 'the keyword routes to a checklist, and a checklist is not a gate' — which is the sharper version of the same point.

missing_classes: documented-triggered-and-still-shipped — the corpus's dominant meta-mechanism, and the taxonomy has no bucket for it. Its why_it_did_not_fire vocabulary offers only four labels (trigger too narrow / scoped to new code / prose nobody opens / gate asserted the wrong thing), all of which presuppose the rule was not reachable. For at least six classes the rule was reachable, the INDEX keyword matched the literal text in the diff, and the rule's own historical-incidents list already contained an identical prior occurrence: time-and-timezone/server-local-trap (two of its six incidents ARE the luxebook#59 and #79 exemplars), observability/analytics-lifecycle-and-containment (its incident #2 is the /me-loading-window reset verbatim), concurrency-cas/async-event-revalidates-live-pointer (its incident is the CoachFlow late-PaymentIntent overcharge), cross-tx-cas-recompute-inside-tx (its round-16 incident is this class's first exemplar), cross-file-seams #1 framework-prefix-doubling (INDEX trigger names `basePath`), webhook-claim-adopt-completedat (INDEX trigger names `webhook` dedupe). The mechanism is not routing at all: a proven prose rule with a correct trigger does not survive contact with a second code site, because reading is optional and nothing re-runs. Every gate_idea in the taxonomy implicitly assumes this class exists; it should be named so the remediation is stated as 'convert to an executable check' rather than 'widen the trigger'.

fix-lands-on-the-path-under-review-not-on-the-family — distinct from any scope language currently in the taxonomy, and it is what actually produced the canonical test case. In channel, 871adff added the atomic finalizeClaim to the OEM path after a Codex P1, hours after 5a043e0 shipped completeUpload without one, in the SAME FILE 890 lines away; the fix was never carried across. luxebook#109 repeats it inside one PR: the identical focus-after-retry defect fixed in tenant-unavailable-view.tsx and left in services-content.tsx. The signature is that the second instance is never in the diff being reviewed, so no diff-scoped process — review, keyword trigger, or blame-driven check — can see it. The craft catalog named it 2026-08-06 (verification-integrity/exhaustive-registry-beats-diff-review, plus the new 'Scope is the FAMILY, not the diff' doctrine) but the taxonomy folds it into scope adjectives on other classes instead of giving it a slug and a registry-enumeration gate.

authority-collision: a project rule prescribes what the reviewer calls a defect — channel/docs/ENGINEERING_CRAFT.md mandates `test.skip(!flag || !hasX(), 'Set VAR=… to run')` for every credentialed suite so absent credentials 'skip cleanly … never fail, never half-run', and the external review then flagged exactly that as absent coverage reading as passing coverage (channel#7). Two authorities give opposite instructions and nothing reconciles them; this defect cannot be fixed by adding a rule, because a rule already requires it. Same shape wherever a design doc, DESIGN.md, or runbook states a policy the reviewer's standard contradicts (luxebook#80's 'do not gate motion, Framer handles prefers-reduced-motion globally'). Needs its own class because the remediation is retraction/reconciliation of an existing authority, not authorship of a new one.

derived-aggregate-maintained-as-a-post-commit-side-effect — a counter, refcount, or rollup is written after the primary transaction commits, so every failure, concurrent delete, or partial batch silently desynchronises it from the rows it summarises, and nothing reconciles. Present across the corpus (channel's publishedRefCount increment/decrement with backfill reconciliation and the double-decrement on concurrent delete; coachflow's bookedCount not restored when NO_SHOW overwrites a just-cancelled booking; luxebook's noShowCount not incremented by applyLateDecision). The taxonomy scatters these into class 3 (rule-in-call-sites) and class 4 (failure-path durability), but neither gate addresses the actual remedy: an idempotent, dry-run-capable backfill that recomputes absolute counts plus a CI assertion that every derived counter has one.
